# Site-specific, explainable anomaly detection for ProtoSense

## Verified facts
- ArmaturaSec reports no malicious examples and acknowledges that historical compromises could have gone unnoticed. Its archives therefore cannot be assumed clean: training and operational calibration must work without attack-labelled examples, not depend on an attack-free guarantee. [F1]
- The company needs site-specific monitoring for both Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP. Its previous classifier generated false positives that led clients to disable alerts; explanations must be understandable to a plant manager. [F2]
- ArmaturaSec says it has on-device inference hardware and uses embedded Linux. Its hardware plan specifies anomaly detection without affecting packet-forwarding latency; actual pilot hardware budgets still need establishing. [F3]
- Company capacity is one to two part-time engineers, with archives, bench and firmware access under NDA. Use of Kiss's group testbed requires a data-sharing agreement. [F4]
- Kiss's Modbus research provides a concrete baseline method using register-level request timing, payload values and function-code sequences. This evidence concerns Modbus/TCP on a substation testbed, not validation on BACnet or ArmaturaSec appliances. [F5]
- Her incremental modelling work found that a planned process reconfiguration produced a persistent anomaly episode. This illustrates a maintenance-related nuisance-alert risk; the work proposed an operator-acknowledged reset. [F6]
- Kiss lists openness to joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions. [F7]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The pilot could show whether useful, understandable alerts are achievable on its own devices without attack-labelled training, and identify whether BACnet support or nuisance alerts block deployment.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement and permissions, Kiss could test how site-specific baselines transfer to BACnet and contaminated operational archives, using permitted captures and controlled bench scenarios.

## Our inference
- A joint project appears well matched: protocol-specific statistical baselines could produce explanations linking an alert to changed timing, values or commands rather than an opaque attack classification.
- The proposal is conditional on confirming Kiss's availability, which is unknown. Openness to joint projects does not establish a commitment of effort.
- BACnet transfer, archive contamination and appliance performance remain experimental gaps. Bench detection could establish bounded scenario coverage, but would not establish recall against unknown operational attacks.

## Proposed next steps
- Propose a six-week pilot using unlabelled client captures, chronological training/calibration/evaluation partitions and an unseen-site evaluation where feasible; check partition independence. Compare fixed-threshold rules with site-specific statistical or one-class models, training and calibrating without attack labels. Test Modbus and BACnet separately, including controlled bench anomalies, legitimate changes and sensitivity to possible baseline contamination. Proposed go/no-go targets for the best configuration, regardless of method: at most one false alert per site-day, at least 80% detection of reserved injected scenarios within 60 seconds, and plant managers correctly explaining at least 80% of sampled alerts. Require authorised access, Yocto on-device execution within agreed CPU/RAM limits, and no measurable forwarding-latency increase at agreed representative loads and measurement resolution. Freeze these negotiation targets before evaluation; report uncertainty and protocol-specific results. Proceed only if both protocols meet the agreed gates without requiring clean-archive guarantees or attack-labelled training/calibration; otherwise revise scope or stop.
- Propose that company engineers select permitted captures, implement feature extraction and profile the target appliance, while Kiss designs baselines and evaluation. Randomly sample across all evaluation windows, including windows with and without alerts, for expert labelling. Compute false-alert rates on reviewed normal windows, count uncertain cases separately, and measure detection only on confirmed or injected cases. Keep evaluation labels out of tuning.
- Subject to available effort, propose weeks one–two for permissions, hardware budgets, representative operating regimes and separate tuning/evaluation samples; weeks three–four for models and safe bench tests; weeks five–six for frozen evaluation and manager review. Test BACnet-specific features and scenarios explicitly, and compare legitimate-change handling with and without operator-authorised baseline updates rather than assuming Modbus results transfer.

## Open questions
- Can Kiss confirm availability and a feasible allocation of research effort for this joint project?
- Can both parties approve client-data permissions, NDA, testbed data-sharing, funding and ownership terms before starting?
- Which pilot appliance and representative traffic loads should define CPU, memory and forwarding-latency acceptance limits?
- Who can approve representative BACnet scenarios, adjudicate uncertain windows and validate the proposed operational acceptance targets with plant managers?

content.title: Serbian-aware retrieval with maintainable vocabulary updates

facts.text: LinguaBot reports that, in a sample of 12,000 real support queries from one bank client, about 18% returned no useful result.

sources.quote: in a sample of 12,000 real support queries from one bank client, about 18% returned no useful result

facts.text: The company's existing Elasticsearch setup uses a Croatian-oriented stemmer that misses Serbian forms. Its users mix Latin and Cyrillic, including within words; integration must therefore address both morphology and mixed-script inputs.

sources.quote: Our current Elasticsearch setup uses a basic stemmer that was built for Croatian and misses a significant share of Serbian-specific forms.
our users freely switch between Latin and Cyrillic script mid-sentence — sometimes mid-word in typos.

facts.text: LinguaBot says manual synonym-list maintenance does not scale with quarterly terminology additions. It requires vocabulary updates without a full re-index.

sources.quote: maintaining those lists manually does not scale as clients add new product terminology every quarter.
can be updated when new vocabulary arrives without a full re-index.

facts.text: LinguaBot has around 85,000 labelled query-response pairs across clients and two linguists who can annotate or validate solutions. Its stated target is a miss rate below 5%, sustained through manageable maintenance.

sources.quote: We have a labelled query-response dataset of around 85,000 pairs across all clients, and our two in-house linguists can annotate or validate proposed solutions.
A good outcome is getting that 18% miss rate below 5% and keeping it there with a manageable maintenance process.

facts.text: The company's tooling/data-work budget is approximately EUR 8,000, and it wants something testable within six months.

sources.quote: Budget for tooling or data work is modest — around 8,000 EUR — and we want something testable within six months.

facts.text: Nikolić's lemmatizer paper describes applying a unified internal representation before lemmatization and restoring the original script afterward.

sources.quote: The proposed system handles both scripts transparently by applying a unified internal representation before lemmatization, then restoring the original script in the output.

facts.text: Her morphological-lexicon study reports 91.3% paradigm correctness for common vocabulary and 78.6% for borrowings.

sources.quote: finding 91.3% paradigm correctness for common vocabulary and 78.6% for borrowings.

inferences: This suggests a plausible joint project linking Serbian linguistic methods to retrieval engineering. The proposal is conditional: Nikolić's participation record indicates openness to joint projects, but her availability and committed effort remain unknown.

Corpus results do not establish performance on banking or telecom support queries, product names or within-word script typos. Lower correctness on borrowings suggests a risk of incorrect expansions; normalization could also merge meaningful distinctions and reduce precision.
proposedActions: First experiment, proposed for months 1–3: reproduce the current Elasticsearch baseline using the 12,000-query sample where accessible. Create separate tuning and held-out evaluation samples from the labelled pairs, checking client, time and duplicate overlap before treating them as independent. Test an explicit matrix: current pipeline; added script normalization only; Serbian lemmatization only; both additions. Include banking, telecom, product-name and within-word-mixing strata. Proposed roles: LinguaBot supplies permitted data, integration and linguist review; Nikolić guides morphology and error analysis. Measure no-useful-result rate, retrieval precision, latency and linguist correction time. Replay new-vocabulary updates and measure re-index operations, effort and post-update miss rate. Go/no-go uses the best configuration tested, regardless of method: below 5% misses overall and after updates, acceptable stratum performance, agreed precision/latency and maintenance limits, no full re-index, and a testable prototype within six months and approximately EUR 8,000 tooling/data spend. These are negotiation targets; unresolved feasibility or unmet criteria trigger revision rather than deployment.

During months 3–5, propose testing paradigm-based query expansion and an external vocabulary layer against the initial configurations. Validate borrowings and ambiguous forms with the linguists. A factor showing no isolated benefit would narrow, not close, the investigation; inspect remaining confirmed misses and test additional interactions.

By month six, propose repeating the frozen evaluation after a terminology update and documenting update effort, regressions and costs. Before starting, agree data controls, commercial-use permissions, artifact access, staffing and responsibility for maintenance; tooling funds should not be assumed to cover research personnel.
questions: Can Nikolić confirm availability and effort for this joint project, and who would fund and perform research, integration, annotation and maintenance?
Which client data and research artifacts may be used under applicable privacy, contractual and commercial-licence conditions?
How is 'no useful result' labelled, and what precision, latency, stratum-performance and maintenance-effort limits should govern acceptance?
Which Elasticsearch version and mappings are deployed, and does 'without a full re-index' permit query-time expansion, external lexicon updates or partial document updates?

benefits.company: The experiment could identify which changes reduce support-search misses and whether terminology updates remain practical without rebuilding the full index.
benefits.researcher: Subject to agreement and permitted access, the project could provide labelled support queries for testing how Serbian morphological methods transfer to commercial terminology and mixed-script inputs.

content.markdown:
# Serbian-aware retrieval with maintainable vocabulary updates

## Verified facts
- LinguaBot reports that, in a sample of 12,000 real support queries from one bank client, about 18% returned no useful result. [F1]
- The company's existing Elasticsearch setup uses a Croatian-oriented stemmer that misses Serbian forms. Its users mix Latin and Cyrillic, including within words; integration must therefore address both morphology and mixed-script inputs. [F2]
- LinguaBot says manual synonym-list maintenance does not scale with quarterly terminology additions. It requires vocabulary updates without a full re-index. [F3]
- LinguaBot has around 85,000 labelled query-response pairs across clients and two linguists who can annotate or validate solutions. Its stated target is a miss rate below 5%, sustained through manageable maintenance. [F4]
- The company's tooling/data-work budget is approximately EUR 8,000, and it wants something testable within six months. [F5]
- Nikolić's lemmatizer paper describes applying a unified internal representation before lemmatization and restoring the original script afterward. [F6]
- Her morphological-lexicon study reports 91.3% paradigm correctness for common vocabulary and 78.6% for borrowings. [F7]

## Potential benefits
- For the company: The experiment could identify which changes reduce support-search misses and whether terminology updates remain practical without rebuilding the full index.
- For the researcher: Subject to agreement and permitted access, the project could provide labelled support queries for testing how Serbian morphological methods transfer to commercial terminology and mixed-script inputs.

## Our inference
- This suggests a plausible joint project linking Serbian linguistic methods to retrieval engineering. The proposal is conditional: Nikolić's participation record indicates openness to joint projects, but her availability and committed effort remain unknown.
- Corpus results do not establish performance on banking or telecom support queries, product names or within-word script typos. Lower correctness on borrowings suggests a risk of incorrect expansions; normalization could also merge meaningful distinctions and reduce precision.

## Proposed next steps
- First experiment, proposed for months 1–3: reproduce the current Elasticsearch baseline using the 12,000-query sample where accessible. Create separate tuning and held-out evaluation samples from the labelled pairs, checking client, time and duplicate overlap before treating them as independent. Test an explicit matrix: current pipeline; added script normalization only; Serbian lemmatization only; both additions. Include banking, telecom, product-name and within-word-mixing strata. Proposed roles: LinguaBot supplies permitted data, integration and linguist review; Nikolić guides morphology and error analysis. Measure no-useful-result rate, retrieval precision, latency and linguist correction time. Replay new-vocabulary updates and measure re-index operations, effort and post-update miss rate. Go/no-go uses the best configuration tested, regardless of method: below 5% misses overall and after updates, acceptable stratum performance, agreed precision/latency and maintenance limits, no full re-index, and a testable prototype within six months and approximately EUR 8,000 tooling/data spend. These are negotiation targets; unresolved feasibility or unmet criteria trigger revision rather than deployment.
- During months 3–5, propose testing paradigm-based query expansion and an external vocabulary layer against the initial configurations. Validate borrowings and ambiguous forms with the linguists. A factor showing no isolated benefit would narrow, not close, the investigation; inspect remaining confirmed misses and test additional interactions.
- By month six, propose repeating the frozen evaluation after a terminology update and documenting update effort, regressions and costs. Before starting, agree data controls, commercial-use permissions, artifact access, staffing and responsibility for maintenance; tooling funds should not be assumed to cover research personnel.

## Open questions
- Can Nikolić confirm availability and effort for this joint project, and who would fund and perform research, integration, annotation and maintenance?
- Which client data and research artifacts may be used under applicable privacy, contractual and commercial-licence conditions?
- How is 'no useful result' labelled, and what precision, latency, stratum-performance and maintenance-effort limits should govern acceptance?
- Which Elasticsearch version and mappings are deployed, and does 'without a full re-index' permit query-time expansion, external lexicon updates or partial document updates?

content.title: Explaining cold-store conveyor weld cracking

facts.text: AutomVoj reports cracking at main crossmember-to-stringer welds after about 18 months. Its frames use painted mild-steel hollow sections, operate in cold stores typically at 2–6 °C, and pass workshop room-temperature load tests. These conditions define the required transfer test.

sources.quote: Our conveyor frames are welded from mild steel hollow section and painted for corrosion resistance before delivery.
typically operating between 2 °C and 6 °C
weld joint cracking at the main crossmember-to-stringer connections after about 18 months of continuous use.
We test frames under load at room temperature and they pass without any problem.

facts.text: AutomVoj has site photographs, crack measurements and two failed sections in storage. Access and a sampling plan preserving material for complementary examinations are therefore prerequisites proposed for this investigation.

sources.quote: We have photos and measurements of the cracked joints from site visits, and we still have two of the failed sections in storage.

facts.text: AutomVoj lacks low-temperature cyclic-testing capability. Erić’s group uses fatigue machines and a climate chamber, but these are shared and extended campaigns require advance scheduling. Combined loading, representative fixtures and condensation control still need confirmation; equipment availability alone does not establish suitability.

sources.quote: We do not currently have the equipment or know-how to test at low temperatures under cyclic load.
The group routinely uses servo-hydraulic fatigue testing machines, a climate chamber capable of reaching −60 °C
Erić's climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared with two other research groups; scheduling access for extended test campaigns requires advance coordination.

facts.text: AutomVoj reports no dedicated R&D department; its chief engineer and two senior automation engineers divide time between live projects and improvement work. Named engineering support must therefore be negotiated rather than assumed.

sources.quote: We have no dedicated R&D department
our chief engineer and two senior automation engineers who allocate time between live projects and improvement work.

facts.text: AutomVoj seeks a causal explanation that enables changes to welding procedure, filler material or joint design, rather than a fatigue-life calculation alone.

sources.quote: understanding exactly what is causing the cracks so we can change our welding procedure, filler material, or joint design

facts.text: Erić’s thermal-fatigue study compared isothermal and combined thermal–mechanical loading in butt-welded S275JR plates. It reported crack-growth behaviour exceeding simple-superposition predictions, supporting controlled comparisons but warning against additive damage assumptions.

sources.quote: butt-welded S275JR plates
Four loading programmes were applied: isothermal fatigue at 20 °C, isothermal fatigue at −30 °C, in-phase thermo-mechanical fatigue (TMF), and out-of-phase TMF
Crack growth rates in both TMF programmes exceeded predictions based on simple superposition of mechanical and thermal stress intensities

facts.text: Erić lists joint projects involving low-temperature or combined-loading fatigue testing among his collaboration interests.

sources.quote: joint projects involving fatigue testing under low-temperature or combined loading conditions

inferences: This suggests a relevant joint project, conditional on confirming Erić’s currently unknown personal availability and equipment slots; his stated openness is not a project commitment.

Transfer remains unvalidated from colder plate-joint studies to painted hollow sections at 2–6 °C. Condensation capability may require external support, and accelerated tests could produce a different failure mechanism.
proposedActions: Propose a first experiment using production-representative painted connections, with separate tuning and evaluation batches whose independence is checked. AutomVoj would supply specifications, specimens and site-monitoring support; Erić would lead failure examination, loading design and testing. Preserve portions of both recovered sections. Measure service strain, vibration, temperature and humidity before fixing exposures. Explicit matrix, holding mean load and geometry fixed: room/dry/reference cyclic load baseline; steady chilled/dry/reference load; service thermal cycling/dry/reference load; room/condensation/reference load; room/dry/reference load plus vibration; combined service thermal cycling/condensation/vibration. Measure cycles to initiation, crack growth, origin, path, fracture appearance and coating damage. Proposed go/no-go: proceed only if the best-tested configuration reproduces the field location and fracture features under service-matched chilled conditions, and controlled contrasts support a testable causal explanation linked to a manufacturing change. No isolated-factor effect would narrow, not end, the mechanism search. Defer if fixtures, environmental control or evidence preservation are infeasible.

Negotiate a staged timeline: two weeks for permissions, evidence review and capability checks, followed by four weeks for service monitoring and specimen planning; schedule testing only after shared-equipment slots are confirmed. Agree specimen counts, replication, uncertainty reporting and a test-duration ceiling before fabrication; these are planning targets, not commitments.

After mechanism matching, test welding, filler or geometry changes individually against the unchanged joint under the best field-matching exposure. As a negotiation target, seek at least 25% greater median cycles to matching crack initiation without a new failure mode. Compare all tested configurations on that metric, then propose field monitoring to assess whether warranty failures actually decline.
questions: Can Erić confirm personal availability, team support and equipment slots, including representative fixtures and controlled condensation capability or an external testing route?
Can AutomVoj authorise evidence access and preservation-led sampling, provide fabrication and coating records, and support monitoring plus matched specimens?
What budget, decision deadline and named company engineering time are available?
What replication, mechanism-match evidence, improvement threshold and field-monitoring duration would both sides require before accepting a production change?

benefits.company: The experiment could distinguish service contributors missed by room-temperature tests and identify whether a specific manufacturing change merits validation, rather than selecting a remedy from an assumed mechanism.
benefits.researcher: Subject to agreement and access, Erić could test whether thermal–mechanical fatigue methods transfer to painted conveyor connections, using recovered failures, service measurements and controlled comparative specimens.
